Here is the full comparison of the four areas you named, plus one packaging change outside them that you'll see in the same diff.

## python_requires

| | v2.31.0 | v2.32.3 |
|---|---|---|
| `python_requires` | `">=3.7"` | `">=3.8"` |
| `REQUIRED_PYTHON` guard | `(3, 7)` | `(3, 8)` |
| Guard message | "pin to an older version of Requests (<2.28)" | "pin to an older version of Requests (<2.32.0)" |

What it means: Python 3.7 is no longer installable. On a 3.7 interpreter, pip reads `python_requires` and will not select 2.32.3, so an unpinned `pip install requests` on 3.7 resolves to 2.31.0 and stays there. The `REQUIRED_PYTHON` block is a separate, earlier guard that only fires when you build from source on an unsupported interpreter; it exits with status 1 before `setup()` runs. The message text was updated to match the new floor, so the advice it prints now points at `<2.32.0` rather than `<2.28`.

## install_requires

No change. Both files define the same four requirements, identical specifiers:

- `charset_normalizer>=2,<4`
- `idna>=2.5,<4`
- `urllib3>=1.21.1,<3`
- `certifi>=2017.4.17`

What it means: upgrading requests itself pulls in no new dependency and relaxes or tightens no existing range. Any dependency churn you see after upgrading comes from the resolver picking newer versions inside these unchanged ranges, not from this file. Note the `urllib3<3` cap was already in place at 2.31.0, so urllib3 2.x was already permitted before this bump.

## extras_require

No change. Both:

- `security: []`
- `socks: ["PySocks>=1.5.6, !=1.5.7"]`
- `use_chardet_on_py3: ["chardet>=3.0.2,<6"]`

What it means: `requests[socks]` and `requests[use_chardet_on_py3]` install exactly what they did before. `requests[security]` remains an empty extra, so it still adds nothing to the install and is safe to drop from a requirements file. The chardet extra is still opt-in, so the default backend stays charset_normalizer.

## classifiers

One removal, one addition, everything else identical:

- Removed: `Programming Language :: Python :: 3.7`
- Added: `Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12`
- Unchanged: 3.8, 3.9, 3.10, 3.11, plus `3`, `3 :: Only`, CPython, PyPy, and the non-Python classifiers (Development Status 5, Apache 2.0 license, Web Environment, etc.)

What it means: the metadata now claims support through 3.12 and drops the 3.7 claim, consistent with the `python_requires` bump. Classifiers are descriptive only; they don't affect resolution. The floor is enforced by `python_requires`.

## Also changed in this file, outside the four areas

The package layout moved to a `src` tree. `package_dir` went from `{"requests": "requests"}` to `{"": "src"}`, and the version read moved from `requests/__version__.py` to `src/requests/__version__.py`. The installed wheel contents are the same; this affects where the source lives in the repo and in an sdist, and it matters if you build from a checkout or vendor the tree.

`test_requirements` is byte-identical between the two.

## Upgrade summary

If you're on Python 3.8 or newer, nothing in this file forces a code or dependency change on you. If you're on 3.7, you cannot install 2.32.3 at all and will stay pinned to 2.31.0 until you move the interpreter.

Scope note: this compares the two `setup.py` files at the two commits you gave. It says nothing about runtime behavior, deprecations, or anything else that changed between the releases.
